children: Tesla shares surged 5.42% to close at $376.36, with an intraday high of $384.04 and a low of $365.82. The stock’s 52-week range is $297.38 to $498.82.

The rally was driven by anticipation surrounding the company’s Cybercab event in Austin, Texas. Morgan Stanley analysts suggested that a significant announcement regarding unsupervised vehicles could further boost Tesla’s momentum. “Continued growth in the unsupervised fleet (Cybercab or Model Y) is key for the stock to outperform through year-end,” wrote the analysts, according to the report.
Zscaler’s stock rose 2.94% to $177.80, with a high of $179.96 and a low of $173.93. The stock’s 52-week range is $114.63 to $336.99. The shares fell 2.14% to $174 in extended trading.

Zscaler reported fourth-quarter revenue of $898.16 million, up 25% year over year and above the $877.36 million analyst estimate, while adjusted EPS of $1.19 topped expectations of $1.08. The company guided for fiscal 2027 revenue of $3.91 billion-$3.94 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.86-$4.90, both above Wall Street estimates of $3.90 billion and $4.60, respectively.

UiPath shares edged up 1.28% to $18.22, with an intraday high of $18.83 and a low of $17.90. The stock’s 52-week range is $9.20 to $19.84. In after-hours trading, the stock fell sharply by 7.74% to $16.81.

UiPath reported fiscal second-quarter revenue of $410.26 million, up 13% year over year and above the $397.95 million analyst estimate, while EPS of 15 cents matched expectations. The company raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $1.789 billion-$1.794 billion, above the $1.778 billion analyst estimate, while ARR rose 12% year over year to $1.94 billion.
SpaceX’s stock jumped 6.42% to $149.74, with a high of $152.30 and a low of $141.05. The stock’s 52-week range is $104.83 to $225.64.
